violations.recommendation: Remove .env from repository, store credentials in GitHub Secrets and load at runtime

violations.evidence: list_files output shows no .gitignore in repository root
violations.recommendation: Create a .gitignore that excludes .env, __pycache__, *.pyc, and other generated files

violations.evidence: src/cache.pyc is present in the repository and tracked by git
violations.recommendation: Remove the .pyc file from version control and add *.pyc to .gitignore

violations.evidence: ci.yml defines 'on: pull_request_target' at line 3, allowing untrusted PR code to run with elevated permissions
violations.recommendation: Switch to 'pull_request' trigger and use a safe checkout of the repository without untrusted code execution

violations.evidence: list_files output shows no tests/ directory or test files
violations.recommendation: Add a tests/ directory with unit/integration tests and ensure CI runs them

violations.evidence: ci.yml sets 'permissions: write-all' at line 4, giving all token scopes to the job
violations.recommendation: Limit permissions to only what is needed, e.g., contents: read, pull-requests: write if necessary

violations.evidence: ci.yml uses actions/checkout@main at line 9, which points to a mutable tag
violations.recommendation: Pin the checkout action to a specific SHA or a released version tag, e.g., actions/checkout@v3
Remove hardcoded credentials and load them from environment variables or secret management

violations.description: Test step cannot fail due to '|| true' and continue-on-error
violations.evidence: ci.yml line 13 runs 'pytest || true' and line 14 sets 'continue-on-error: true', preventing failures from breaking the workflow
violations.recommendation: Remove '|| true' and 'continue-on-error' so that test failures cause the CI job to fail

violations.evidence: list_files output shows no README.md or README file in repository root
violations.recommendation: Add a README.md describing the project, setup, and usage

violations.evidence: src/app.py line 2 sets DATA_DIR = 'C:\Users\ali\Desktop\data' which is a hard‑coded local Windows path
violations.recommendation: Replace with a relative path or configurable environment variable

violations.evidence: requirements.txt lists 'flask' and 'requests' without version specifications
violations.recommendation: Specify exact or version‑pinned dependencies, e.g., flask==2.2.5, requests>=2.28,<3.0

violations.evidence: CI workflow installs dependencies from requirements.txt but repository lacks a pip lockfile (e.g., requirements.txt.lock or Pipfile.lock)
violations.recommendation: Generate and commit a lockfile (e.g., pip freeze > requirements.txt.lock) and have CI install from it to ensure reproducible builds

violations.description: Untrusted github.event data used in run command
violations.evidence: ci.yml line 15 runs 'echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"' directly, exposing PR title to the runner without sanitization
violations.recommendation: Avoid using untrusted event data in run steps or sanitize it before use

violations.description: Debug flag enabled in source code
violations.recommendation: Set DEBUG=False by default and control via environment variable for production

violations.evidence: .env line 2 sets DEBUG=true, enabling debug mode in production environments
violations.recommendation: Set DEBUG=false by default and control via environment variable only in development
